_doc: Registry of every hydra automation that can APPROVE Muso credit requests without a human choosing each request. scripts/check-credit-approval-automation.sh (CI: scripts/tests/check-credit-approval-automation.bats) fails if a cron in cron-jobs.json calls one of these entrypoints without being registered here, or is enabled while its entry has approved=false. dispatch-cv-batch.sh reads approved for credit-verification-batch and forces DRY (zero writes) unless it is true. Flipping approved to true is a captain decision: set approved_by and approval_ref (who said yes, and where) in the same PR.

credit-verification-batch.description: Lobster credit-verification pipeline (verify-credit-batch-mvp.lobster): approves signal_approve rows and moves the rest to user_verification_needed. Reached by the credit-verification-batch-4h cron and by the @Ops 'run credit verification' / 'verify profile' / 'verify credit' Slack triggers.
credit-verification-batch.status_note: DISABLED 2026-10-11 (firstmate containment, captain standing order 'we can't let bad credits into the system'). Its approve rule (approve_owning_track == 100 AND total_risk_percent < 80) was inverted: 100 means the validator's owning-track shortcut did NOT fire, so the rule approved validator-DECLINED rows with risk 30-80. Real apply stays blocked until the captain approves the fixed pipeline.

credit-trust-decide.description: scripts/credit-review.py decide --mode apply (cron credit-trust-decide-15m): trust-yet-verify on the held (unverified) queue. Provisionally approves non-big rows with no validator conflict that have ONE evidence kind (all roles trusted-confirmed, a trusted footprint of >= 3 confirmed claims in each claimed role family, or Codex on server-fetched sources with verified quoted citations on >= 2 independent domains, never crowd-edited MusicBrainz/Wikipedia alone; editorial roles only on trusted catalog confirmation under pop 30), and moves the rest to user_verification_needed (Knock asks the user for proof). The fraud/PULL/HOLD/RE-VERIFY lists in policies/credit-trust-decide.json are never approved. Writes only via muso-admin-api.sh's conditional endpoint as credit-trust-decide@hydra-ops; the wrapper re-checks this entry at the write boundary and core-backend's agentApprovalGuard refuses any row with a validator conflict.

Support writes are capped at 100 distinct users per run and max_ask_users_per_day per day, ledgered as the `decider-support` ask so the tick's own campaigns stand down, and every apply run owes a read-back before the next. This PR adds no cron: arming is an ops step (docs/credit-verification/decider-support-arm.md). Paging alert: scripts/credit-decider-support-watch.py.

Every other guard intact: no validator conflict, no reject_* rule, core's approval guard clear (band A; band B only after core's phase-1 twin is live, Fable 2026-10-20; a band-hint-only proof stamp is not an open ask unless the user engaged: proof on file, support email, Intercom conversation), popularity known, > 0 and < 60, no organization/label/publisher/studio role, user and profile not on the decider's deny/fraud/PULL/HOLD lists, per-user daily approval cap. Ledger before write (decisions.evidence_kind validator_low_risk); writes via the decider's conditional PUT (expected = the row's own held status, caps and pause re-checked under the write lock before every batch) as credit-trust-decide@hydra-ops; reversible per run (credit-review.py revert --run, named human). Provisional: verify-notify candidates (one v1 note).

fable-decider.description: L12 executor (scripts/credit-fable-execute.py), never scheduled. Carries out Fable-ruled tray files on disk where EVERY row carries a Fable ruling id (else the whole tray is refused). TWO scopes: (1) CLOSES (action reject): unverified / user_verification_needed -> rejected, on the decider account (MUSO_ADMIN_IDENTITY=credit-decider) with X-Credit-Automation-Id fable-decider; guards on fresh Postgres facts: same status and user, not deleted, the cited reject_* still fires or a Fable R- rule with evidence, known not big (pop 1..59, not client-sourced), no live claim by the submitter on the profile, account gate allow, not watchlisted; cap 100/day (<= 400 only with a Fable cap ruling id). (2) APPROVALS (action approve; core FABLE_RULED scope, core #11010/#11011): unverified / user_verification_needed / rejected -> approved on Fable's OWN login (MUSO_ADMIN_IDENTITY=fable = agent-fable@muso.ai), admitted by core ONLY on a server-held fresh anchor record (credit_anchor_records, written by the DSP verifier's identity) on every claimed role, pinned in the approving UPDATE; executor guards: same status and user, known-small pop 1..59, account gate allow, not watchlisted; label-path approvals provisional 7 d; cap 50/day, counted separately from closes. Both: kill file /etc/hydra/fable-decider.disabled + this registry entry re-checked before every batch and at the wrapper boundary (verify_batch on a clean env), <= 100 ids per close call / <= 50 per approve call, read back from Postgres, one audit line per row (/var/lib/hydra/credit-review/fable-decider-audit.jsonl), stops on the first surprise. Never deletes.

document_small_track.description: [key=doc-approval-doctrine] Fable R22 (2026-11-05 20:2xZ, data/verify-sla-driver-fable-d2/ruling-R22-doc-only-approval.md): the document_small_track approval class - scripts/credit_review/doc_approve.py plus the decide.py approved_refs write. A FORGERY-CHECKED (dv-4 verified) document may approve a small-track credit WITHOUT a same-run DSP anchor. T0/T1 only (popularity 1-59; UNKNOWN = big = NO); T2/T3 keep the replacement message. Under EIGHT CODED guards, never a per-item ruling: forensics (h3 PLAUSIBLE with an extracted issuer/signatory) AND an independent cross-check positive with none contradicting; same_release (xc_dsp on this track or xc_isrc by ISRC); role (not contradicted at a trusted source, and not artist/org); claimant (clean >= 30 days or a prior approval); scope document_small_track; PROVISIONAL 7 days never lowered; caps 1/request, 5/user, 10/profile, 50 users/day, fail-closed; 100% audit for 14 days with auto-freeze on a SINGLE reversal and the requester told. Order: paid first, oldest document first. Code: hydra #1684 + the R22 delta PR. Consumed by t01b's executor and by decide.py's own class check (decide.doc_class_approved).

Kill switch /etc/hydra/doc-approve.disabled. A later contradicted/forged verdict PULLS a provisional approval (recorded, then a named human's own session does the core reversal - agent tokens are refused on the admin credit DELETE routes) and FREEZES the class until a human clears /var/lib/hydra-credit-verify/doc-approve.frozen.

credit-removal-executor.description: scripts/clickup_drain/credit_removal.py + scripts/credit_review/removal_executor.py: clears ClickUp `action:credit-removal` tickets through the TWO intents of the credit-removal model (Fable credit-removal-flow-fable-r2 §4/§7). `hide_mine` ('this is me, but hide it from my profile') writes the served-visibility hide only: no verification, no catalog delete, reversible (unhide). `not_me` ('this isn't me / I'm not on this track') files a removal claim on the core removal gate, which hides the credit at once and decides on the deterministic public-credit rule; this automation never decides a removal and never calls a catalog delete. A proof follow-up is recorded in `credit_proof_verifications` and graded by ONE tool-less Codex call (credit_trust.llm.Provider; the metered OpenRouter rung is the shared ladder every other credit judgement uses), and the graded proof is POSTed to the gate's own proof route as evidence on the EXISTING claim (once per request+proof, never re-filing the claim); until that route exists the ticket says `proof_awaiting_gate` (proof received, graded X, awaiting gate) and the internal ask for proof is not repeated. Identity comes from the verified Intercom contact through credit_review.identity_resolver, never from the ticket text. Every write is a line in /var/lib/hydra/credit-removal/ledger.jsonl with an inverse (unhide / withdraw) and is replayable with `--revert <run_id>`.
credit-removal-executor.status_note: SHIPS UNAPPROVED, on purpose. Three separate gates must open before a credit is hidden or a claim is filed: (1) THIS entry must be flipped to approved:true with the captain's approved_by + approval_ref, because a hide is customer-visible on a named person's profile and the first batch is signed off from the dry run (one line per ticket: intent, track, roles, identity match and the disposition); (2) /etc/hydra/credit-removal-executor.live must exist, because the core routes it calls are new (C1's hide primitive, C2's gate request) and a human has to record that core really admits this automation; and (3) the routes must actually answer: while C1/C2 are unmerged every row is `authority_unavailable` (the run reports it and writes nothing) rather than falling back to the legacy removal path. Kill switches: /etc/hydra/clickup-drain-credit-removal.disabled (the drainer), /etc/hydra/credit-removal-executor.disabled (the executor), the cron's enabled:false, and this flag. Caps: 20 rows/run, 3 rows/ticket. The two intents are the ONLY actions; the cron ships dry-run.

verification-scale-drain.description: The verification scale drain (scripts/credit_review/scale_drain.py): a deterministic SQL ladder over the 92,861-request verification backlog, no model in the hot path. Approves ONLY on a row-specific evidence anchor - a per-claimant precedent match (the same claimant's earlier approved request for the same track and role set) or a proof verdict (the proof id, newest verdict wins including a soft one) - closes a decided duplicate, and queues a refusal or an asked-and-expired request for a named tier-2 approver. A row with no anchor falls through to ask. Writes through the reviewed wrapper (PUT /admin/credit-requests) under its own requester identity scale-drain@hydra-ops, admitted by is_scale_drain_approval in muso-admin-api.sh, which re-checks this registry entry, the kill file /etc/hydra/scale-drain.disabled, the body shape (<=50 unique UUIDs) and the drain-signal digest naming an auto-approvable rule. Never sets CV_APPROVE_GATE_DISABLED. Never lowers a served number, never deletes, never removes a credit.

proof-review-coded.description: scripts/ops_intake/proof_review.py review --mode apply: answers a 'review the proof' ask from H3 + doc-verify + dsp-verify + the fraud lens. Registered here anyway so a future cron that runs it can never slip past this guard.

Turning that on is a captain decision and a reviewed PR that also sets approved/approved_by/approval_ref here.
